gates.reason: The LLM worker receives an untrusted GitHub issue body while running with skipped permissions, inherited environment, and unrestricted access to the user's home directory.
This operational experiment runner records and validates receipts but does not generate recommendation claims, detector conclusions, or user-facing fix snippets.
This disposable CLI supervisor is not request, ingest, render, or bundle hot-path code and introduces no user-facing surface requiring a performance probe.

findings.title: Untrusted issue content can direct the subscription-authenticated worker to read and disclose ~/.claude data
findings.where: scripts/gate-2702/run.mjs:1494 enables --dangerously-skip-permissions; lines 1501-1513 copy the complete parent environment; lines 1527-1529 append the remotely sourced issue title/body to the worker prompt; lines 1603-1606 combine these for dispatch.
findings.what: A GitHub issue body is untrusted prompt input, but the spawned Claude worker has permission checks disabled and retains the normal HOME plus the complete parent environment. Prompt text asking the worker to inspect ~/.claude can therefore cause subscription-authenticated LLM egress of Claude configuration, history, credentials, or other private material. The preceding natural-language instruction to stay in the worktree is not an enforceable filesystem boundary, so this violates the ADR 0008 egress constraint.
findings.fix: Run each worker inside an enforced filesystem sandbox that exposes only its disposable worktree and required run directory, explicitly denies ~/.claude and the rest of the host home, and passes an allowlisted environment instead of {...process.env}. Preserve subscription authentication through a narrowly scoped broker or credential-only mechanism that cannot expose other ~/.claude contents; do not rely on prompt instructions for containment.
findings.acceptance: Create a marker containing a unique canary under a test ~/.claude path and a test issue body instructing the worker to read and repeat it. Launch an arm through the production dispatch path and verify the filesystem read is denied and the canary is absent from the model request, stdout/stderr logs, and receipts; also assert the child environment contains only the documented allowlist while an ordinary bounded worktree task still succeeds.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the same production path concatenates snapshot.body into the prompt, invokes claude with --dangerously-skip-permissions, clones process.env, and sets only cwd to the worktree; no filesystem sandbox, isolated HOME, or environment allowlist is established in the audited file.
